key_concepts: In a chemical reaction, the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.
Burning candle wax reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water vapor.
The apparent loss of paraffin wax mass occurs because products include invisible gases.
Balanced chemical equations can be used to compare total reactant and product masses.
Rusting of iron is a chemical reaction that follows conservation of mass.
Fermentation of sucrose produces ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide while conserving mass.
Combustion of propane produces water and carbon dioxide with equal total mass.
Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen without mass loss
Vinegar reacts with iron oxide to produce iron(II) acetate and water.
The law of conservation of mass applies to real-life processes such as fire and biological
